newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-LARA LEADS WEST INDIES TO STUNNING WIN.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-LARA LEADS WEST INDIES TO STUNNING WIN.

text.p: Brian Lara scored his first century on tour as the West Indies beat Australia by seven wickets in a high-scoring limited overs international on Sunday.
Lara made a scintillating return to his dominating best in scoring 102 to steer West Indies to victory in their World Series encounter with seven balls to spare at the Gabba.
Chasing Australia's daunting 281 for four in 50 overs, West Indies comfortably reached 284 for three on the strength of Lara's efforts and an equally impressive century by Carl Hooper.

Hooper, batting one place below his vice-captain at number four, abandoned his early supporting role once Lara was out to take responsibility during the final overs. Fittingly, he hit the winning runs to finish 110 not out.
After looking badly out of sorts for several weeks, Lara finally found his timing and placement in a purposeful innings that featured two sixes and eight fours.
Hooper and Lara shared a third wicket partnership worth 154 runs off just 167 deliveries.
The result was a disappointing outcome for Australia opener Mark Waugh, who matched Lara's achievement by scoring 102 before being run out.
All-rounder Stuart Law contributed 93, joining with Waugh to add 145 runs for the second wicket after Australia won the toss in ideal batting conditions.
It was a highly impressive run chase by West Indies, who have reversed their fortunes after losing the opening two matches in the competition.
Only New Zealand, who amassed 297 to beat England in Adelaide 14 years ago, have recorded a higher winning total batting second in a one-day interanational on Australian soil.
West Indies lead the triangular tournament with six points from three victories in five games.
Australia, who have lost nine of their last 11 one-day internationals at home and abroad, have four points. Pakistan also have four points but have played one game less than their rivals.
